chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu Abd al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Do not leave the prayer deliberately, for whoever leaves it deliberately, the religion of Islam has disavowed him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of deliberately neglecting prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) concise advice to a companion, emphasizing that deliberate neglect of Salat is the primary marker of apostasy. This hadith is central to the Shia juristic debate regarding whether leaving prayer constitutes major unbelief (kufr akbar) or a lesser form, with many scholars citing it as evidence for the former due to the explicit phrase 'bari’at minhu millat al-Islam' (the religion of Islam is disavowed from him). It underscores the structural primacy of prayer in maintaining the integrity of one's faith identity within the Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Al-Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Al-Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to the Prophetsaww, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! Advise me’. So hesaww said: ‘Do not leave the Salāt deliberately, for the one who neglects it deliberately, so the nation of Al-Islam is disavowed from him’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy from al-Qaddah who has said

the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that a man came to the Holy Prophet asking, ‘O Messenger of Allah, give me a good advice.’ He said, ‘You must not give up Salah (prayer) intentionally; the community of Islam is free from all obligations toward one who gives up Salah (prayer) intentionally.’”
